newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks recover momentum, close firm.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks recover momentum, close firm.

text.p: Argentine stocks bounced back from a dull patch Thursday and were seen stretching gains as the week draws to a close, dealers said.
"The bolsa's positive tone was boosted today by the rally in U.S. markets," said Dario Lizzano, head of research at Santander Investments.
"U.S. retail sales data confirm interest rate worries are fading, and our economy remains very healthy, especially thanks to rising tax collection," he added.
The blue-chip MerVal index rose 1.4 percent to a new five-year high of 814.50.
It was little changed in the previous two sessions, and markets were closed Monday for a national holiday.
"Today we saw institutional players return and fuel last week's gains," one trader said. "However, because next Monday is another holiday, we may not be able to keep up this pace."

Floor volume swelled by 10 million pesos from Wednesday to 39.5 million pesos, matching last week's daily average, while over-the-counter turnover rose more moderately to 96.9 million pesos from 82.5 million Wednesday.
The MerVal rose 7.7 percent in May and stands 4.7 percent higher so far this month.
The broad market index closed up 1.2 percent Thursday, with winners bashing losers 67 to 12, and 12 issues closing flat.
Top main-tier performers were oil company Astra, real estate developer Irsa, and construction stock Juan Minetti, which surged 4.7 percent, 4.2 percent and 3.8 percent, respectively.
The only MerVal losers were carmaker Sevel, which shed 2.3 percent, and electricity generator Central Costanera, off 2.2 percent.
